mainTopic: Blood and other discharges from the מקור: when they make a woman טמאה, where the inner boundary lies, and רבי שמעון's rule about discharging שכבת זרע
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation of a ברייתא about blood that comes with a יוצא דופן. רב יוסף rejects that explanation and says the argument is whether the womb (מקור) is itself a טמא place, even when the blood leaves through the side. ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן then argue whether the woman herself becomes a נדה in that case. רבי יוחנן says she does not, because a woman is a נדה only when the blood leaves through her ערוה. Next come rulings about a womb that falls out and about pearl-like drops from the womb. Both bring only טומאת ערב, not seven days of נדה. The גמרא then defines the בית החיצון, where blood already makes a woman טמאה while it is still inside her, and a ברייתא learns this from the word ״בבשרה״. Finally it discusses רבי שמעון's rule that a woman discharging שכבת זרע is no more טמאה than the man. The גמרא resolves a contradiction in his words and ends with a question about רבא's three-day rule for a woman who had relations.

steps.title: Finishing the first explanation: baby through the side, blood the normal way
steps.stepSummary: The earlier explanation of the ברייתא ends here. The baby came out through the side, the blood came out through the womb, and each side follows its own view about יוצא דופן.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and the blood came out through the womb. So רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning, and the רבנן follow theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an explanation that started before this section. The case is a baby born through the side with blood coming out the normal way, and each side's ruling comes from its known view on יוצא דופן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a יוצא דופן counts as a real birth, so blood that came out in the days before it is treated as birth-related and is טהור. The רבנן hold that a יוצא דופן is not a halachic birth, so that blood is ordinary זיבה blood and is טמא. With this reading the ending of the ברייתא needs no new idea, because it just repeats the known argument.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born through a cut in the side of the belly, like a C-section
Through the womb, meaning the normal way out of the body
He follows his own reasoning, consistent with a view he holds elsewhere

phrases.english: and the blood through the womb,
and Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning
and the Rabbis follow their own reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַזְדָּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְטַעְמֵיהּ וְרַבָּנַן לְטַעְמַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an explanation of the ברייתא that started before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case so it fits each side's known view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ending of the ברייתא seems to need its own explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a case of a baby through the side and blood through the womb, and each side follows its view on יוצא דופן.

steps.title: רב יוסף's two problems with that explanation
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives two problems. The explanation makes the ending of the ברייתא repeat the opening, and the word 'from there' points to where the baby came out, not to the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected. First, that is the same as the opening clause. Second, 'from there' means from the place the baby came out!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the explanation from step 1 with two separate problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Problem one: if the case is just about יוצא דופן counting as a birth, the ברייתא already taught that argument at the start, so the ending would add nothing. Problem two: the ברייתא says the blood came out 'מִשָּׁם', from there, which refers back to the place already mentioned, the opening in the side. In step 1 the blood came out the normal way, so that does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly challenged it
One problem… and another problem
The first part of the teaching
From there, pointing back to a place already mentioned

steps.confusionAlert: 'From there' does not mean the womb. רב יוסף says it means the opening in the side where the baby came out.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected to it:
One — that this is the same as the first clause,
And furthermore — 'from there' implies the place of the baby!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the baby came out through the side and the blood through the womb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes the ending of the ברייתא repeat the opening, and it goes against the word 'מִשָּׁם', which points to the opening the baby came out of.

steps.title: רב יוסף's new case: baby and blood both through the side
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains the ending of the ברייתא differently. Both the baby and the blood came out through the opening in the side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead, רב יוסף said: it is a case where the baby and the blood both came out through the side.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף replaces the explanation from step 1 with a new case that solves both of his problems. This also sets up the next step, which explains what the two sides are really arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'מִשָּׁם' fits, because the blood came out from the same place as the baby. The ending also no longer repeats the opening, because the question is now about blood that never left the normal way at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, the word that brings a replacement explanation
For example, a case where
The baby or offspring

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
for example, where the baby and the blood came out
through the side,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two problems from step 2 by defining a new case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The blood came out through the womb, the normal way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both the baby and the blood came out through the side.

steps.title: The real argument: is the womb itself a טמא place?
steps.stepSummary: In רב יוסף's case the argument is about מקור מקומו טמא. The תנא קמא says the womb is a טמא place, so its blood is טמא however it comes out. רבי שמעון says it is טהור, so only blood that leaves the normal way makes her טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about whether the place of the מקור is טמא. One Sage holds that the place of the מקור is טמא, and the other holds that it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the idea behind the two rulings in רב יוסף's case. This finishes his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא holds that the womb itself is a טמא place, so blood from it is טמא even when it leaves through the side. רבי שמעון holds that the womb is a טהור place, and blood only makes a woman טמא when it comes out the normal way. So blood through the side is טהור in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'source', meaning the womb or uterus
The womb is itself a טמא place, so its blood is טמא wherever it exits
They argue about
Ritually pure

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, the ברייתא's ending is about blood that comes out through the side. The תנא קמא says it is טמא because the womb is a טמא place. רבי שמעון says it is טהור because the womb is a טהור place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This creates a new rule that matters beyond the case of יוצא דופן: is blood טמא because of where it comes from, or because of the way it leaves the body?

phrases.english: and they argue about whether the place of the source is impure;
phrases.notes: 'Source' here means the womb.

phrases.english: one Sage holds: the place of the source is impure,
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, who rules the blood טמא.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: the place of the source is pure.
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון, who rules the blood טהור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the idea behind the two rulings in רב יוסף's new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is whether the womb is a טמא place: the תנא קמא says yes and רבי שמעון says no.

steps.title: Is the woman herself טמאה when the blood is טמא?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the woman's status follows the blood's status. רבי יוחנן says that even when the blood is טמא, the woman stays טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: according to the one who says the blood is טמא, the woman is also טמאה, and according to the one who says the blood is טהור, the woman is also טהורה. רבי יוחנן says: even according to the one who says the blood is טמא, the woman is טהורה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are still on רב יוסף's case, where the blood left through the side. The blood itself is טמא according to the תנא קמא, and now two אמוראים argue about whether the woman herself becomes a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate questions here: is the blood טמא, and is the woman a נדה? ריש לקיש links them, so if the blood is טמא then she is a נדה too. רבי יוחנן separates them, so the blood can be טמא while the woman stays טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says the blood is טמא (the תנא קמא)
The one who says the blood is טהור (רבי שמעון)
Says the woman herself is טמאה as a נדה

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the blood and the woman apart. The blood can be טמא (it passes טומאה to whatever it touches) while the woman herself is not a נדה.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
According to the one who says the blood is impure,
he says the woman is impure too,
and according to the one who says the blood is pure,
he says the woman is pure too.
But Rabbi Yochanan says:
Even according to the one who says the blood is impure,
he says the woman is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לְדִבְרֵי הַמְטַמֵּא בַּדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב יוסף's case and the argument over מקור מקומו טמא, and asks what this means for the woman herself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: the woman's status follows the blood. רבי יוחנן: even when the blood is טמא, the woman is טהורה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's view matches his rule from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן is consistent. He taught in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי that a woman is a נדה only when her blood leaves through her ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning. He said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: where do we learn that a woman is not טמאה until her flow leaves through her ערוה? The פסוק says: 'A man who lies with a woman who is דוה, and uncovers her ערוה, he has exposed her מקור.' This teaches that a woman is not טמאה until her flow leaves through her ערוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן said the woman stays טהורה. It points to another teaching of his, which says נדה only applies when the blood leaves the normal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק connects the woman's flow (דוה) to her ערוה. So טומאת נדה needs the blood to leave through the ערוה. In our case the blood left through the side, so the woman is not a נדה, even if the blood itself is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Her flow (menstrual blood)
Through her ערוה, the normal way
A woman who has her flow, a נדה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rule behind רבי יוחנן's view: what makes a woman a נדה is the path the blood takes, not only where the blood comes from.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
From where do we know that a woman is not impure
until her flow comes out through her nakedness?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכַּב אֶת אִשָּׁה דָּוָה
phrases.english: As it says: 'And a man who lies with a woman having her flow,

phrases.aramaic: וְגִלָּה אֶת עֶרְוָתָהּ אֶת מְקוֹרָהּ הֶעֱרָה״,
phrases.english: and uncovers her nakedness, he has exposed her source,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:18

phrases.english: this teaches that a woman is not impure
until her flow comes out through her nakedness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind רבי יוחנן's view in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the woman stays טהורה even if the blood is טמא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His teaching in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, based on ויקרא 20:18, that נדה only applies when the flow leaves through the ערוה.

steps.title: A womb that fell out makes the woman טמאה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה, teaches that if a woman's womb comes loose and falls to the ground, she is טמאה, and learns it from a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: if the מקור came loose and fell to the ground, she is טמאה, as it says: 'Because your foundation was poured out and your nakedness was uncovered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, related rule about the מקור (the womb). If it detaches and falls out, the woman becomes טמאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of something 'poured out', which is read as the womb falling out, and calls it an uncovering of ערוה. This shows the womb still counts as a source of טומאה even after it has left the body. At this point we are not yet told what kind of טומאה this is. That is the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: That was uprooted or came loose
Your 'foundation', read here as the womb

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:
A womb that came loose and fell to the ground,
she is impure,
as it says: 'Because your foundation was poured out,
and your nakedness was uncovered.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 16:36

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching connected by topic: the מקור and the טומאה that comes from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the womb detaches and falls out, the woman is טמאה.

steps.title: What kind of טומאה can this be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of טומאה the woman has. It cannot be seven days of נדה, because the תורה says נדה comes from blood, not from a piece of flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what kind of טומאה? If you say seven-day טומאה, the תורה said 'blood', not a piece of flesh!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to know exactly how טמאה she is. It first tests the obvious answer, seven days of נדה, and rejects it. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven days of טומאת נדה comes from blood, as the פסוק says. A womb that falls out is a piece of flesh, not blood. So it cannot make her a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? (what does this apply to)
If you say (a suggestion that is about to be rejected)
Seven-day טומאה of a נדה
A piece of flesh

phrases.english: For what?
If you say for seven-day impurity,
the Torah said 'blood',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:19

phrases.english: and not a piece of flesh!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the ruling in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What level of טומאה the woman gets when her womb falls out.

steps.title: Only טומאה until evening
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that she has טומאת ערב, a one-day טומאה that ends at nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is for טומאה until evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer: the woman is טמאה only until evening, not for seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since it cannot be נדה, her טומאה is a lighter kind that ends at nightfall. She gets it because her body touched the womb, which is a source of טומאה, as the פסוק in step 7 taught.

keyTerms.meaning: טומאה that lasts until nightfall

steps.whatToRemember: A womb that falls out does not make a woman a נדה, because נדה needs blood. It only makes her טמאה until evening.

phrases.english: Rather, it is for impurity until evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The woman has טומאת ערב, not seven days of נדה.

steps.title: Two pearl-like drops from the womb make her טמאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if the מקור releases two clear, pearl-like drops, the woman is טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: if a woman's womb lets out two drops that look like pearls, she is טמאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי יוחנן. It continues the theme of טומאה that comes from the מקור without regular blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These drops are not red blood. They look whitish and clear, like pearls. Still, רבי יוחנן says the woman becomes טמאה, which raises the question of what kind of טומאה this is.

keyTerms.meaning: Sweated out or discharged a little moisture
Pearls; here, clear whitish drops that look like pearls

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
A womb that discharged
phrases.notes: Literally "sweated." It means a small amount of moisture came out.

phrases.english: something like two pearl-like drops
— she is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling. Like the fallen womb, this is טומאה from the מקור that is not normal blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two pearl-like drops from the מקור make the woman טמאה.

steps.title: Which kind of טומאה is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of טומאה the drops cause. It cannot be seven-day נדה, because only five blood colors are טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what kind of טומאה? If you say seven-day טומאה, that can't be, because there are only five kinds of טמא blood in a woman and no more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which kind of טומאה רבי יוחנן means. It rules out the first option, seven days of נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A known rule says only five colors of blood make a woman a נדה. Pearl-white is not one of them, so these drops cannot bring seven-day טומאה. This is the same pattern as step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: The five colors of blood that are טמא
And no more

phrases.english: For what [kind of impurity]?
If you say for seven-day impurity,
— there are five kinds of blood that are impure in a woman
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה earlier in this מסכת (נדה 19a) that lists the five colors.

phrases.english: and no more!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It clarifies the type of טומאה in רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the drops bring seven-day נדה טומאה or a lighter טומאה.

steps.title: It is טומאת ערב, and only with two drops
steps.stepSummary: The answer is טומאת ערב. Two drops are needed, because a single drop might have come from somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is טומאה until evening. And this is only with two drops. With one drop, I can say it came from somewhere else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the drops cause only a one-day טומאה. It also explains why רבי יוחנן said "two" drops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anything from the מקור makes her טמאה until evening, even if it is not blood. With only one drop, we cannot be sure it came from the מקור at all, so she stays טהורה. Two drops show it really came from the מקור.

keyTerms.meaning: Specifically, exactly
It came from elsewhere, not from the מקור

steps.whatToRemember: Pearl-like drops from the מקור bring only טומאת ערב, never נדה, and only when there are at least two drops.

phrases.english: Rather, for impurity until evening.
And this is specifically with two [drops],
but with one,
— I can say it came from elsewhere.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question in step 11 and adds the two-drop condition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She has טומאת ערב, and only when there are two drops.

steps.title: What is the outer chamber?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that women become טמאה in the בית החיצון and asks where exactly that is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: all women become טמאה in the outer chamber. Which place is the outer chamber?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for a definition. This step sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once blood reaches the בית החיצון, the woman is טמאה even if the blood has not yet left her body. So we need to know exactly where that area begins.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer chamber, the outer part of the woman's body where blood makes her טמאה
Which is it? What is it?

phrases.english: All women become impure
in the outer chamber.
phrases.notes: This line is a quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: Which is the outer chamber?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It begins a new section about the משנה's term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact boundary of the בית החיצון.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the place seen when a girl sits
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש defines the בית החיצון as the area that can be seen when a young girl sits.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: any place that can be seen when a young girl sits.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives his answer. The outer chamber is the part that can be seen from outside when a girl sits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By his definition, the outer chamber is only the very outer area. Blood would have to reach a fairly visible spot before she becomes טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl
Is seen, is visible

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
Any place that is seen when a young girl sits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כֹּל שֶׁתִּינוֹקֶת יוֹשֶׁבֶת וְנִרְאַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first answer to the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בית החיצון is the area visible when a girl sits.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: that place already counts as exposed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן objects that the area ריש לקיש describes already counts as an exposed part of the body for טומאת שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: that place counts as exposed even for touching a שרץ!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שרץ only makes a person טמא if it touches an exposed part of the body. The area ריש לקיש describes is already treated as exposed, like the outside of the body. So the משנה would not need a special rule for blood there. The בית החיצון must mean a place further inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Exposed, counted as the outside of the body
A dead creeping creature that makes a person טמא by touch

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
That place is considered exposed
with regard to a creeping creature!
phrases.notes: His point: a place that already counts as "outside" can't be what the משנה needed to teach us about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם גָּלוּי הוּא אֵצֶל שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It attacks ריש לקיש's definition.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's definition of the בית החיצון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The area he describes already counts as exposed for שרץ, so it cannot be the special inner area the משנה is defining.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: up to בין השינים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives his own definition: the outer chamber reaches as far as the area between the teeth-like folds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן says: up to "between the teeth."
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected ריש לקיש, רבי יוחנן offers his own answer to the question in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view the בית החיצון goes deeper, up to the teeth-like folds inside the body. So blood makes her טמאה even before it reaches the visible area.

keyTerms.meaning: Between the teeth, meaning teeth-like folds inside the woman's body

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan says:
Up to "between the teeth."
phrases.notes: These "teeth" are teeth-like folds inside the body, not real teeth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עַד בֵּין הַשִּׁינַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It replaces ריש לקיש's rejected definition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בית החיצון extends up to בין השינים.

steps.title: Is the area between the teeth inside or outside?
steps.stepSummary: A question is raised: does the area בין השינים itself count as inside or as outside?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: is "between the teeth" itself like inside or like outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the exact edge of רבי יוחנן's boundary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said "up to" בין השינים. That leaves it unclear whether the boundary spot itself belongs to the outer chamber, which would make her טמאה, or to the inside.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised for them
Like inside
Like outside

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Between the teeth itself —
is it like inside or like outside?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בֵּין הַשִּׁינַּיִם כְּלִפְנִים אוֹ כְּלַחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks about the exact edge of רבי יוחנן's definition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the boundary area בין השינים itself counts as inside or outside.

steps.title: רבי זכאי: between the teeth counts as inside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי זכאי settles it. The outer chamber reaches up to בין השינים, but the area between them counts as inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רבי זכאי teaches: up to between the teeth; between the teeth themselves is like inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Up to" here means "not including." Blood that is only between the teeth is still counted as inside, so she is not yet טמאה. Only blood past that point, in the outer area, makes her טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Themselves

steps.whatToRemember: The בית החיצון goes up to בין השינים, but the area between the teeth itself counts as inside.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Zakkai teaches:
Up to between the teeth;
between the teeth themselves is like inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It resolves the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The area בין השינים itself counts as inside.

steps.title: A ברייתא names the point as 'the place of threshing'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives another description of how far inside the blood must reach: the מקום דישה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: the place of threshing.
steps.whatsHappening: After the definitions of ריש לקיש, רבי יוחנן and רבי זכאי, the גמרא quotes a ברייתא that uses a different phrase for the boundary: 'מקום דישה'. This phrase is unclear, so it sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps argued about where the בית החיצון ends. This ברייתא gives its own description of the point blood must reach. It is a polite, indirect phrase, so it needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: In a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself)
'The place of threshing', a polite indirect phrase for a spot inside the body

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא:
The place of threshing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different ברייתא's wording for the inside/outside boundary discussed in steps 14-18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood makes her טמאה once it reaches the 'מקום דישה'.

steps.title: What does 'place of threshing' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase מקום דישה refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'place of threshing'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unclear phrase from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is being challenged here. The phrase is indirect, so the גמרא asks which exact spot it means.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? (asking for the meaning of a term)

phrases.english: What is the 'place of threshing'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the term quoted in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which spot inside the body the phrase מקום דישה refers to.

steps.title: רב יהודה explains the phrase
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says it is the place the male organ reaches during relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: the place where the שמש threshes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains that 'מקום דישה' means the spot that is reached during marital relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the image of threshing as a modest way to say this. Once blood reaches that spot, it counts as being in the בית החיצון, and she is טמאה even though it has not yet left her body.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'servant'; a polite word for the male organ
Threshes; here, reaches or presses against

phrases.english: רב יהודה said:
The place where the שמש threshes.
phrases.notes: 'שמש' is a polite word for the male organ. He means the spot it reaches during relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מְקוֹם שֶׁהַשַּׁמָּשׁ דָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מקום דישה is the spot reached during relations.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן rejected ריש לקיש's 'what is seen when she sits' and set the boundary at בין השינים, with the area between them counting as inside. A ברייתא describes the point as 'מקום דישה', which רב יהודה explains as the spot reached during relations.

steps.title: ״בבשרה״: נדה and זבה are טמאה even while the blood is still inside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״בבשרה״ that blood still inside her makes her טמאה, both as a נדה and as a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'In her flesh' teaches that she becomes טמאה inside just as outside. This tells me only about a נדה. How do I know it for a זבה? The verse says 'her flow in her flesh'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא. It shows from the פסוק that a woman becomes טמאה once blood reaches the בית החיצון, even before it comes out of her body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the source for the whole topic of the inner area. The word ״בבשרה״ means 'while still in her flesh'. The words ״זובה בבשרה״ extend the same rule to a זבה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In her flesh', the word in ויקרא 15:19 the דרשה is built on
Inside just as outside
A woman in her regular monthly period
A woman with bleeding outside her regular days
The verse comes to teach (introduces the word the rule is learned from)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'In her flesh' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:19

phrases.english: teaches that she becomes impure inside just as outside,
and I have only a menstruating woman;
a זבה, from where do we know?
The verse says: 'Her flow in her flesh.'
phrases.notes: The verse's word is ״זובה״, 'her flow', which sounds like זבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the rule that blood inside already makes her טמאה, which steps 14-21 have been taking for granted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both a נדה and a זבה become טמאה once the blood reaches the בית החיצון, even before it comes out of the body.
steps.whyThisMatters: This דרשה is the reason the definitions of the בית החיצון matter at all.

steps.title: ״יהיה″: discharging שכבת זרע also makes her טמאה from inside
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא learns from ״יהיה״ that a woman discharging שכבת זרע is also טמאה before it comes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who discharges semen, from where do we know? The verse says 'shall be'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It extends the 'inside counts like outside' rule to a woman discharging שכבת זרע, learning it from the extra word ״יהיה״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood is the topic of the פסוק, so a separate source is needed for שכבת זרע. The ברייתא takes the extra word ״יהיה״ as including this case too.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who discharges semen after relations
'Shall be', an extra word in the פסוק used to include another case

phrases.english: A woman who discharges semen, from where do we know?
The verse says: 'shall be.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of step 22 to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman discharging שכבת זרע is טמאה even while it is still inside her.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: she is no more טמאה than the man
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds דיה כבועלה: just as the man is טמא only once the זרע comes out, she is טמאה only once it comes out of her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: it is enough for her to be like the man who was with her. Just as he does not become טמא until the impurity comes out, so too she does not become טמאה until her impurity comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the ברייתא about the שכבת זרע case. He says she becomes טמאה only when it comes out of her body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic: the זרע came from the man, and the man is טמא only after it comes out. So her טומאה should not be stricter than his. He does not argue about blood, only about שכבת זרע.

keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for her to be like the man who was with her (she is not stricter than him)
Just as ... so too (a comparison pattern)
Outside (out of the body)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון disagrees only about שכבת זרע. He is not arguing about blood of a נדה or זבה, where everyone agrees inside counts like outside.

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון says: It is enough for her to be like the man who was with her —
just as the man who was with her does not become impure
until the impurity comes outside,
so too she does not become impure
until her impurity comes outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the דרשה of ״יהיה״ in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman discharging שכבת זרע becomes טמאה only once it comes out of her body.

steps.title: Does רבי שמעון really hold דיה כבועלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי שמעון holds דיה כבועלה and starts quoting a ברייתא that seems to show otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי שמעון really hold that it is enough for her to be like the man? But it was taught: 'They shall bathe in water and be impure until evening.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's view. It begins quoting a ברייתא that explains the פסוק about a man and woman becoming טמא through relations, which sets up the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word והתניא signals that another teaching seems to contradict what רבי שמעון just said. The quoted פסוק is the starting point of that teaching, and its explanation comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he really hold...? (opening a challenge)
And they are impure until evening

phrases.english: And does רבי שמעון hold that it is enough for her to be like the man who was with her?
But wasn't it taught:
'They shall bathe in water and be impure until evening,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:18

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דַּיָּהּ כְּבוֹעֲלָהּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי שמעון's position from step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's rule of דיה כבועלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא records רבי שמעון explaining the פסוק of ״ורחצו במים״ in a way that will seem to contradict דיה כבועלה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון asks what the פסוק comes to teach
steps.stepSummary: In that ברייתא, רבי שמעון asks what the פסוק adds. Touching שכבת זרע is already covered by ״או איש״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: What does this come to teach us? If it is about touching semen, it already says below: 'or a man'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון's own analysis. He asks why this פסוק is needed, since touching שכבת זרע is already taught elsewhere. His full answer, which creates the contradiction, comes in step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון rules out one possible purpose of the פסוק: teaching that touching זרע makes one טמא. That is already learned from ״או איש״ in ויקרא 22:4. So the פסוק must be teaching something new about the woman, and that new point is what the גמרא will use against him.

keyTerms.meaning: What does this come to teach us? (asking why a פסוק is needed)
One who touches semen
Below, later in the תורה

phrases.english: רבי שמעון said:
And what does this come to teach us?
If it is about one who touches semen —
it is already said below: 'or a man.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:4

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: וְכִי מָה בָּא זֶה לְלַמְּדֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted as the source of the challenge in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון learns a separate טומאה for the woman from ״ורחצו במים״
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's analysis in the ברייתא: touching זרע is already covered by ״או איש״ in ויקרא 22:4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's rule of דיה כבועלה (step 24)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון shows the פסוק ״ורחצו במים״ is not needed to teach that touching זרע makes one טמא, since ״או איש״ already teaches that. So it must teach something new about the woman. Step 27 spells out what that is.

steps.title: The תורה decrees that hidden contact makes her impure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes: the פסוק is needed because contact inside the body normally does not make a person טמא, and here the תורה decrees that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק is needed because this is contact with impurity in a hidden part of the body. Contact in a hidden part normally does not make one טמא, but here it is a special decree of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי שמעון's ברייתא. He explains that the פסוק comes to teach that a woman becomes טמאה from זרע even though the contact happens inside her body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally טומאת בית הסתרים, contact in a hidden part of the body, does not make anyone טמא. רבי שמעון says the תורה makes an exception here, so she is טמאה while the זרע is still inside her. That clashes with דיה כבועלה from Step 24, where he said she is טמאה only once it comes out.

keyTerms.meaning: Contact with impurity in a hidden, internal part of the body
A decree of the פסוק, a rule the Torah sets even without a logical reason
Does not make one impure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the general rule. Hidden contact usually does NOT make one טמא. This case is a special exception that the תורה creates.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁטּוּמְאַת בֵּית הַסְּתָרִים הִיא,
phrases.english: Rather, because it is impurity in a hidden place,
phrases.notes: He means that during relations, the זרע touches her inside her body, not on the outside.

phrases.english: and impurity in a hidden place does not make one impure,
but it is a decree of the פסוק!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁטּוּמְאַת בֵּית הַסְּתָרִים הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 26 and gives the punch line of the challenge from Step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds a woman is טמאה from זרע while it is still inside her, which goes against דיה כבועלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's ברייתא reading the פסוק as a גזרת הכתוב about hidden contact
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's rule of דיה כבועלה (step 24)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this ברייתא רבי שמעון reads the פסוק as a גזרת הכתוב that hidden, inside contact with זרע makes the woman טמאה. That contradicts his statement that she is טמאה only once the טומאה comes outside.

steps.title: During relations versus a later discharge
steps.stepSummary: No contradiction: the ברייתא about hidden contact deals with a woman during relations, while דיה כבועלה deals with a woman who discharges זרע afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is talking about a woman during relations, and there it is talking about a woman who discharges afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two statements of רבי שמעון are about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the act of relations itself, the תורה's decree makes her טמאה even from inside contact. When she later discharges זרע, דיה כבועלה applies, so she is טמאה only once it comes out, just like the man.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer that splits the cases.
A woman having marital relations
A woman discharging זרע after relations

steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction between משמשת and פולטת drives the rest of the discussion.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, with a woman who has relations,
phrases.notes: This "here" is the ברייתא from Steps 26-27 about hidden contact.

phrases.english: there, with a woman who discharges.
phrases.notes: This one is the דיה כבועלה statement from Step 24.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא — כָּאן בִּמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת, כָּאן בְּפוֹלֶטֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Steps 25-27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): two different situations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements of רבי שמעון seemed to address the same situation, so they appeared to contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: During relations she is טמאה even from inside contact. After a later discharge, she is טמאה only once the זרע leaves her body.

steps.title: She is already impure from the relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a discharging woman is already טמאה because she had relations, so why discuss her discharge at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who discharges? Derive her impurity from the fact that she had relations!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Any woman who discharges זרע must have had relations first, so she is already טמאה anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the relations already made her טמאה, the question of when the discharge makes her טמאה seems pointless. So the case of a פולטת in Step 24 needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it from elsewhere. You already know it from another reason.
She had relations

phrases.english: A discharging woman? Let him derive it
from the fact that she had relations!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case of פולטת used in the answer of Step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of פולטת in Step 28
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פולטת already had relations and is טמאה from that, so the timing of the discharge's impurity changes nothing.

steps.title: She already immersed for the relations
steps.stepSummary: The case is where she already went to the מקוה to purify herself from the relations, and only afterward discharged.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where she immersed to purify herself from her relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the discharge case is about a woman who has already cleaned up the impurity of the relations by immersing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she has immersed, the relations no longer make her טמאה. So a later discharge is a new source of impurity, and then it matters that she becomes טמאה only once it comes out.

keyTerms.meaning: She immersed in a מקוה
Her relations

phrases.english: Where she immersed for her relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פולטת is always still טמאה from the relations.
steps.terutzMaskana: After immersing, the relations' impurity is gone, so the discharge is a separate issue.

steps.title: Can one immersion really be enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether immersing and waiting until evening is enough after relations, since רבא says she cannot eat תרומה for three days because she will surely discharge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that for a woman who had relations, impurity until evening is enough? But רבא said: a woman who had relations may not eat תרומה for all three days, because she cannot avoid discharging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that her immersion fully solves the impurity of relations. It brings רבא, who says she stays unable to eat תרומה for three days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 suggested that she immerses and is טהורה by evening. רבא says that for three days she will certainly discharge זרע and become טמאה again, so she cannot eat תרומה. That suggests one immersion does not settle her status. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? This opens a challenge drawn from what was just said.
It is enough for her
The portion of produce given to a כהן. It may be eaten only in טהרה.

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's rule about three days of possible discharge is a practical הלכה for a woman who eats תרומה.

phrases.english: Is that to say that for a woman who had relations
impurity until evening is enough for her?
But didn't רבא say:
A woman who had relations, for all three days
is forbidden to eat תרומה,
since it is impossible for her not to discharge.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דִּמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת בְּטוּמְאַת עֶרֶב סַגִּי לַהּ? וְהָא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 30, which assumed one immersion ends the impurity of relations.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in Step 30 that immersion leaves a משמשת with only impurity until evening
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא rules that she cannot eat תרומה for three days because discharge is certain, so one immersion and evening should not be enough.

steps.title: She was immersed while lying in bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is a woman who was immersed in bed, so she did not walk and the זרע stayed inside her.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? A woman whom others immersed while she was still in bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from רבא by describing a special case: other people immersed the woman while she was still lying in bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a woman cannot eat תרומה for three days after relations because she will surely discharge. Here she stays lying down, so her immersion does purify her from the relations themselves. Any זרע that comes out later can then make her טמאה again, which is exactly the case of דיה כבועלה.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to narrow a statement to a specific situation
They immersed her: others performed the immersion for her
Bed

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
Where they immersed her in the bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבא's three-day rule in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After relations a woman always discharges, so immersing right away never helps.
steps.terutzMaskana: If she is immersed while lying in bed, the זרע can stay inside. Her immersion purifies her from the relations, and a later discharge is a separate new טומאה.

steps.title: Then why would רבא's walking woman still be טמאה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רבא was talking about a woman who walked to the מקוה, and asks: maybe all the זרע came out while she walked.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that when רבא spoke, he meant a woman who walked on her own feet to immerse. But maybe while she was walking she already discharged everything?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the last answer and draws a conclusion about רבא's case. It then challenges that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If lying in bed is what keeps the זרע inside, then רבא's three-day rule must be about a woman who walked to the מקוה. But walking should push the זרע out. So why would she still be expected to discharge later and stay טמאה for three days?

keyTerms.meaning: By inference: it follows from this that
On her own feet
Perhaps, maybe
She threw it out, meaning she discharged the זרע

phrases.english: By inference, when רבא said it
phrases.notes: This refers to רבא's rule from step 31: no תרומה for three days after relations.

phrases.english: it was where she herself walked on her feet and immersed.
Perhaps while she was walking, she discharged it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the answer in step 32 and uses it to challenge רבא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a woman is טמאה for three days after relations because she will surely discharge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If walking is what pushes זרע out, then a woman who walked to the מקוה may have already discharged everything on the way, so there is no reason to fear a discharge afterward.
